observations: Photo 0 shows a white industrial sewing machine mounted on a metal table with a flat work surface.
The machine has a beige and white body, with a control panel, three spool pins on top, and a foot pedal connected by a cord.
There is a red circular logo on the front, but the brand name is not legible.
Photo 1 shows the same machine from a slightly different angle, with a metal arm extending over the machine, possibly for lighting or thread guidance.
The background is a rough brick wall with some white chalk writing (numbers) visible in photo 1.
The machine appears to be in a workshop or storage area, with no visible fabric or active use.
No power cord is visible in either photo, and no indication of whether the machine is plugged in or operational.

claims.evidence: The photos show an industrial sewing machine, not a weaving machine. Weaving machines are structurally different and typically larger, with loom frames and shuttle systems, which are absent here.
An industrial sewing machine is indeed suitable for textile production and fabric work, even if the seller misidentified it as a weaving machine.

risks.risk: Machine may not be functional or may have mechanical issues
risks.proof: A video showing the machine powered on and stitching fabric, or a close-up of the motor and needle in motion.

risks.risk: Missing or damaged parts (e.g., power cord, foot pedal, accessories)
risks.proof: A full view of the machine with all components laid out, including the power cord and any attachments.

risks.risk: Hidden wear or damage to internal mechanisms (e.g., motor, gears)
risks.proof: A close-up of the motor housing, belt, and needle bar area, or a video of the machine running.

proof_requests: Video of the machine in operation, stitching fabric.
Photo showing the power cord and foot pedal.
Close-up of the machine's brand and model label, if any.
Photo of the entire machine from all angles, including underside and back.
response.reason: The item is clearly an industrial sewing machine, not a weaving machine as claimed. While it is suitable for textile production, its functionality, completeness, and condition are unverified. Without proof of operation and full component set, it cannot be priced accurately.
